title: The dialog Element and Popover API
summary: Show temporary content using browser features designed for overlays.
nestedConcepts: Name the control and its purpose
Choose a non-modal popover when appropriate

subtopics.title: Open a modal with showModal()
subtopics.explanation: Calling `dialog.showModal()` opens a dialog above the page and makes the rest of the document inactive for interaction. This is useful when a decision must be handled before returning to the page. Include a clear close action and ensure focus returns to the control that opened it.

subtopics.title: Use the browser top layer
subtopics.explanation: Dialogs opened with `showModal()` and shown popovers enter the browser’s top layer, which sits above ordinary stacking contexts. This avoids many `z-index` conflicts. A non-modal dialog opened with `show()` does not block the page, so choose the behavior that matches the interaction.

subtopics.title: Name the control and its purpose
subtopics.explanation: Give a dialog or popover a useful heading and connect that heading as its accessible name when needed. A person should know what the panel is for before acting. For an icon-only trigger, provide a label on the button that opens the panel.

subtopics.title: Manage keyboard focus
subtopics.explanation: When a modal opens, move focus to an appropriate control inside it and keep keyboard navigation within the modal. On close, return focus to the opener. Test Escape behavior, visible focus, and screen-reader announcements rather than relying on the panel’s appearance alone.

subtopics.title: Choose a non-modal popover when appropriate
subtopics.explanation: Use a popover for lightweight content that should appear above the page without blocking the rest of it, such as a help panel or action menu. Use a modal dialog when the user must respond before continuing. Outside-click dismissal and keyboard behavior should match the purpose of the content.

foundations.overview: The dialog element creates a dialog that can be opened modally or non-modally. The Popover API displays temporary content without manually managing every overlay detail. These features still need clear labels, focus behavior, and sensible dismissal controls.
foundations.mentalModel: A dialog is a conversation that pauses the room; a popover is a note beside a control.
foundations.whyItMatters: Native browser behavior reduces custom overlay code and improves consistency.

keyTakeaways: The browser manages a top layer for dialogs and popovers.
Use a clear accessible name and purpose.
Keep keyboard focus usable and predictable.
Choose popover for lightweight non-modal content.
